sources.title: Cellular energetics lecture.pdf
sources.text: ATP hydrolysis releases free energy when ATP reacts with water to form ADP and inorganic phosphate. Cells couple this favorable reaction to processes that require energy. ATP is regenerated from ADP and phosphate using energy from other reactions.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains how ATP provides energy for cellular work?
choices: ATP hydrolysis releases free energy, and cells couple that reaction to energy-requiring processes.
ATP stores energy only after it is broken down into ADP and phosphate.
ATP is regenerated by using energy from other reactions, but hydrolysis itself does not release energy.
ATP and water react to form more ATP directly during energy transfer.
hints: Look for the option that mentions ATP breaking down with water.
The key idea is energy release from hydrolysis, then coupling to work.
questions.workedExample: If a cell needs energy for a process, it can link that process to ATP breakdown so the released energy helps drive it.

questions.prompt: What is regenerated when a cell uses energy from other reactions to rebuild ATP?
hints: Think about what must be rebuilt to make ATP again.
